passage:
Warden's note, hostel B. Harish came to my room on Sunday evening looking unsettled. He explained that his partner Tara has a close friend, Ojas, who calls her late in the evenings and whom she has known since school. Harish said he felt uneasy each time the phone lit up with Ojas's name and wasn't sure whether the unease was fair.

He told me he had thought of saying, "Choose between us," and knew that would be wrong. He was rubbing the back of his neck as he spoke.

Instead, he decided to invite Ojas for chai with Tara, and to tell Tara, "I feel uneasy sometimes, and that's mine to work on. I'm not asking you to give him up." I said that sounded fair, and that I was around if he wanted to talk again.

qa.q: How long has Tara known Ojas?
qa.a: Tara has known Ojas since school.

qa.q: What does Harish's rubbing the back of his neck suggest?
qa.a: It suggests he is uncomfortable and unsure, since he says he knows an ultimatum would be wrong yet still feels uneasy when Ojas calls.

qa.q: What did Harish plan to do about his uneasiness, and why might it work?
qa.a: He planned to have chai with Ojas and Tara and to tell Tara his feeling is his to work on, which gets him to know Ojas without forcing Tara to choose.

qa.q: How might Tara see it if Harish told her to choose between him and Ojas?
qa.a: She might feel pressured and hurt, and see it as being told which friendships she is allowed to keep.

grounding: Shows uneasiness about a partner's close friend, met with getting to know them and sharing the feeling instead of an ultimatum.

passage: Ada had been best friends with Tomasz since primary school in Leeds, long before Emeka came along. They had inside jokes Emeka didn't understand, a Friday film night, and a way of finishing each other's sentences that made his stomach tighten. Twice he'd almost said, 'Maybe you should see less of him.' He knew how that would land: as an order. So one Sunday, walking back from the market, he said instead, 'Can I tell you something a bit embarrassing? I feel insecure about Tomasz. It's not anything he's done. You two just have so much history.' Ada squeezed his arm. 'Thank you for telling me. Why don't you come to film night?' He went. Tomasz had made terrible popcorn and an even worse pun about it. By the end of the evening the two of them were arguing happily about football. Walking home, Emeka realised the unease had shrunk to something small and ordinary.

qa.q: How long had Ada and Tomasz been best friends?
What was Emeka feeling about Ada and Tomasz's closeness?
qa.a: He felt insecure, his stomach tightening at their shared history and inside jokes.

qa.q: What did Emeka do instead of asking Ada to see less of Tomasz?
qa.a: He shared his feeling honestly and then got to know Tomasz at film night.

qa.q: How does Ada respond to Emeka's confession?
qa.a: She thanks him and invites him to film night, including him rather than defending herself 😊

grounding: Shows a young man uneasy about his partner's close male friend, sharing the feeling and getting to know him instead of ordering distance.

passage: At the university research lab where they all worked, Ujjwal's girlfriend Anjali spent long afternoons at the next bench with Tenzin, her project partner and closest friend from undergrad. They shared earphones while running experiments and laughed at pipette jokes nobody else found funny. Ujjwal, working two rooms away, felt a knot of unease every time he passed the glass door. One evening he drafted a message: 'Either you switch partners or we need to talk.' He looked at it for a long time. It was an ultimatum, and he knew it. He deleted it. At the lab's Friday tea, he pulled up a stool next to Tenzin instead and asked about the project. Tenzin turned out to be shy, obsessed with mountain birds, and planning to propose to his own girlfriend in Sikkim. Later Ujjwal told Anjali, 'I've been feeling insecure about you two. Talking to him helped.' She hugged him. 'Thank you for not making me choose.'

qa.q: What did Ujjwal feel each time he passed the glass door?
qa.a: A knot of unease and insecurity about Anjali's closeness with Tenzin.

qa.q: What did Ujjwal do instead of sending the ultimatum?
qa.a: He deleted it, got to know Tenzin at Friday tea, and then shared his feeling honestly with Anjali.

qa.q: How does Anjali respond when Ujjwal tells her?
qa.a: She hugs him, grateful he didn't make her choose.

grounding: Shows a young man insecure about his partner's close male friend, rejecting an ultimatum, getting to know him and sharing the feeling honestly.
